dedupe_keys.name: nsw spatial digital twin and sdt explorer

description: The NSW Spatial Digital Twin (SDT) is an ecosystem of platforms, data and services that gives a shared, near real-time 4D view of New South Wales for government, industry and the community. At its core are the Spatial Collaboration Portal, which stores and manages more than 1,000 datasets from government agencies and lets everyone search and discover them, and the SDT Explorer, a free web tool for 3D and 4D visualisation, location intelligence and scenario modelling. The Explorer shows detailed models of buildings, infrastructure and landscapes over time, connects to live sensor, traffic and environmental data, runs development and emergency response scenarios, and offers web maps and dashboards; experienced users can build their own models, run analyses and create reports. Agencies and councils use it for urban planning, asset management, environmental monitoring, emergency management and public engagement, and a Policy Framework sets the rules for submitting and using data. Coverage: New South Wales, using actual building locations, infrastructure and property boundaries. Access: free Explorer in a browser; a products and services catalogue (PDF, January 2026) is linked. Licence: dataset terms set by data custodians under the Policy Framework. Caveats: the older spatial.nsw.gov.au project page blocked automated readers, and which datasets are public was not checked. Simulation uses: building-level exposure, planning and emergency scenarios on a state-wide 3D base. Related records: Virtual Singapore and the Sydney urban form data.
